title: Harnessing the Power of Generative AI to Support ALL Learners
extended_summary:
This exploratory paper examines how teachers perceive generative AI, especially ChatGPT, as a tool for supporting multilingual learners and students with disabilities through Universal Design for Learning (UDL). The authors were interested in whether teachers viewed ChatGPT as helpful or harmful, what benefits and drawbacks they associated with it, and how it might be used to support language learning and accessibility.

The study was conducted during a summer 2023 professional development institute with 137 educators, including elementary, secondary content, ESOL, special education, pre-service teachers, administrators, and other school staff. Participants all worked with multilingual learners in suburban school districts in the Mid-Atlantic region of the United States. Data came from plenary-session polls, small-group workshop artifacts, and teacher reflections, followed by descriptive summarization and categorization of perceived benefits and drawbacks within UDL principles.

Findings were entirely perceptual rather than outcome-based: teachers were split on whether generative AI was a "friend" or "foe," and many believed it could improve accessibility, language support, translation, feedback, and differentiated materials, while also raising concerns about cheating, bias, reduced critical thinking, and overreliance. The paper does not test student achievement or reading/literacy outcomes and does not report subgroup comparisons for emergent readers, multilingual learners, or students with disabilities beyond qualitative, teacher-reported implications. Its main conclusion is that generative AI may help teachers create more flexible UDL-aligned materials for multilingual learners, but further research is needed.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI’s generative AI chatbot/large language model system for natural-language generation, question answering, drafting, translation, and feedback generation.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as the focal generative AI tool in a teacher professional development study. Teachers explored ChatGPT 3.5 for lesson planning, generating tables, creating responses to writing assignments, creating factual questions, providing feedback on writing, lowering reading level, adding citations, translating responses, and discussing how it could support multilingual learners and UDL.

findings.finding_summary: This exploratory study did not test student outcomes. Among 137 teachers working with multilingual learners, 43% agreed or strongly agreed before the ChatGPT workshop that ChatGPT and other generative AI would help make instruction more accessible for all learners (including those with disabilities), while 23% disagreed/strongly disagreed and 32% were undecided. After exploring the tool, teachers generated more positive (54%) than negative (46%) perceived aspects, but these were perception data rather than literacy outcome data.
findings.measure: Teacher perceptions of accessibility/support for multilingual learners and perceived benefits/drawbacks

quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative/exploratory professional development study with teacher perception data, not a controlled evaluation of student literacy outcomes. The paper includes no subgroup outcome analyses or causal estimates.
impact_tier_rationale: No effect size or student outcome impact is reported. The paper suggests potential accessibility benefits for multilingual learners and students with disabilities, but only at the level of teacher perceptions and brainstormed uses.
